label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Thanks, Deirdre, for asking for my thoughts rather than just announcing it, and for acknowledging what Noma and I have built in that room.

I understand the numbers. With 24 children in Grade 00, Bronwyn needs the help more, and I’m not asking you to reverse the allocation. I’m also grateful that Noma will only be across the courtyard, not gone altogether. But I’d be pretending if I said I wasn’t gutted. She’s been with me in the Seahorses for three years, since my first year teaching. In some ways she trained me — from the sign-in sheets to the parent WhatsApp group — and she knows my children in a way that can’t be captured on an allocations sheet. In Term 2, when Zayd had his meltdowns, she was the one who could calm him, sitting with him under the jungle gym. And the children ask for “Noma’s song” at morning ring every day.

My main worry is the first few weeks of Grade R: new children crying at the gate, new routines, and a new assistant all at once. I’d like to ask SMT for two things to make the handover gentler:

- Could Charlene come in for a day or two during 1–4 December, before she officially starts on 11 January, to meet Noma, see the routine and go through the practical handover properly?
- Could Noma pop in for morning ring during the first week back from 14 January, even for just 15 minutes? She could help hand over her isiXhosa songs to Charlene and give the children some continuity. Luthando and Mia already know her from aftercare, so her presence could help settle them too.

I’m not trying to hold on to Noma or make this harder for anyone. I just want the children, Charlene and Noma to have a proper handover, rather than an abrupt change on the first day. Thank you for listening and for taking this to SMT.
